questions.stem:
Fig. 1 shows a measuring cylinder containing water. Fig. 2 shows the same measuring cylinder after a stone has been lowered into it.
[Fig. 1, Fig. 2: diagram not included]

lines.label: a
lines.text: Calculate the volume of the stone. [2]

lines.label: b
lines.text:
Another stone has a mass of 98.4 g. The volume of this stone is 41.0 cm³. Calculate the density of the stone.
density = ______ g/cm³ [3]

lines.label: c
lines.text: The stone with a mass of 98.4 g has a weight of 0.984 N. Explain the difference between mass and weight. [2]

questions.stem:
Fig. 1 shows a coil of wire.
[Fig. 1: diagram not included]

lines.label: a(i)
lines.text:
A student measures the length of the coil using a ruler. His measurement is 3.8 cm. There are 20 turns of wire in the coil. The student uses his measurement to calculate the average thickness of the wire.
Show that the average thickness of the wire is about 0.2 cm. [2]

lines.label: a(ii)
lines.text:
A student measures the length of the coil using a ruler. His measurement is 3.8 cm. There are 20 turns of wire in the coil. The student uses his measurement to calculate the average thickness of the wire.
The student's measurement of 3.8 cm is inaccurate. Suggest one reason why the measurement is inaccurate. [1]

lines.label: b
lines.text:
The volume of the wire in the coil is 16.6 cm³ and its mass is 148 g. Calculate the density of the metal used for the wire in the coil.
density = ______ g/cm³ [3]

lines.label: c
lines.text:
The student has a measuring cylinder and a beaker of water, as shown in Fig. 2.
[Fig. 2: diagram not included]
Describe how the student can determine the volume of the coil by using the equipment shown in Fig. 2. [4]

lines.label: a(i)
lines.text:
The mass of the mercury in the thermometer is 12 g.
Calculate the weight of the mercury.
weight of mercury = ______ N [3]

lines.label: a(ii)
lines.text:
The mass of the mercury in the thermometer is 12 g.
The 12 g of mercury has a volume of 0.88 cm³. Calculate the density of mercury.
density of mercury = ______ g/cm³ [3]

lines.label: b(i)
lines.text:
The mercury in the thermometer expands when its temperature rises.
State what happens to the mass of the mercury when its temperature rises. Tick (✓) one box: mass decreases / mass stays the same / mass increases.

lines.label: b(ii)
lines.text:
The mercury in the thermometer expands when its temperature rises.
State what happens to the density of the mercury when its temperature rises. Tick (✓) one box: density decreases / density stays the same / density increases.
